clue.text: Colours, which is normal

definitions.meaning: a regiment's colours are its flag
normal as an adjective means usual or conventional, the accepted level

explanation.surface: Someone asks which shade of paint counts as the ordinary one.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimental flag is carried as its standard, and the same word as an adjective means typical or usual.

clue.text: Fringe report

definitions.meaning: in American English hair cut straight across the forehead is called ...
a report is the loud noise of a gun or explosion

explanation.definitionFit: Hair cut across the brow is a bang in American usage, and a gunshot's sharp noise is a bang too.

clue.text: About mid-December an excellent player appeared

indicators.note: the player's word sits about, that is around, the middle letters

parts.note: a top player in a tournament is seeded, a seed

indicators.note: mid- takes the central letters of the word December

explanation.surface: Around the middle of December a star performer turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: A seed is a highly ranked player in a tournament draw; 'About' is the container signal, not a word for concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemed and appeared both mean gave the impression of being.

clue.text: People after an apart, ment find there's competition

indicators.note: after places the people's word behind the flat in the finished answer

parts.note: a flat is the British word for an apartment
a race is a people, a group sharing descent

explanation.surface: Flat-hunters discover that others are chasing the same property.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed text splits 'apartment' with a stray comma. A flat race is a horse race run without jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race run without fences or hurdles is a contest, a kind of competition.

clue.text: Capital is available for the laundry to a point

parts.note: washing is the clothes waiting to be laundered
N, north, is one of the points of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone advertises a laundry service delivered right to a particular spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington DC is the capital city of the United States.

clue.text: A man from Andover none will employ

indicators.note: the words Andover none take on, that is contain, the name inside them

explanation.surface: A man from a Hampshire town is someone nobody will hire.
explanation.walkthrough: Andover is a town in Hampshire; the name runs across the end of 'Andover' and the start of 'none'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernon is a man's first name, so a man is a fair general description.

clue.text: Ships' rats seem revolting

definitions.note: the possessive apostrophe reads as ships are, plural vessels

indicators.note: revolting means rising up in rebellion, so the letters of rats seem are overturned

explanation.surface: The rats aboard a vessel look disgusting, or are in mutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' rearranges RATS SEEM. The apostrophe in 'Ships'' works as 'Ships are'.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam-powered vessels are ships, so the plural noun fits.

clue.text: Stay in when broke. That's common sense

indicators.note: when broke means once broken up, so the letters of stay in are smashed and reset

explanation.surface: Advice to stay home when penniless, which is only sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when broke' rearranges STAY IN; 'broke' looks like a word for penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound judgment, a sane mind, is what we call common sense.

clue.text: The person who's put in charge

definitions.text: The person who's put in charge

parts.words: The person who's put in charge
parts.note: reads as a manager given authority, but means one who puts a charge of powder or shot into a gun

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loads a firearm with its charge of ammunition does exactly what the clue says.

clue.text: Compact made, weapons must be turned over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the weapons word is read backwards

parts.note: guns are weapons

explanation.surface: A treaty is signed, and arms must be handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be turned over' turns GUNS round; 'Compact' looks like a noun for a pact but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug describes something closely fitting and neat, compact in size.

clue.text: On the watch, with little to pass on

parts.note: minute means tiny, little
to hand something is to pass it on

explanation.surface: A lookout on duty has little to report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the watch' looks like being on guard, but points to a part found on a watch face.
explanation.definitionFit: The longer pointer on a timepiece dial sits on the watch, telling the minutes.

clue.text: Directed police offensive

parts.note: to run a business is to direct it, so ran is directed
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A police operation was ordered to go on the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like a noun for an attack but is the adjective for a foul smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid food smells or tastes stale and foul, which is offensive.

clue.text: A rival can not admit being investigated

indicators.note: admit means let in, so the can not word takes the investigated phrase inside

parts.note: can not is shortened to can't
something under examination is on test

explanation.surface: A competitor refuses to confess while under scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admit' sets ON TEST inside CANT after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone entering a competition is a rival to the others in it.

clue.text: Exercise is sound-fall in!

indicators.note: in puts the falling word inside the sound word

parts.note: a ting is a light ringing sound
rain is a fall of water from the sky

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant's order: the exercise is to fall in properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective for healthy and 'fall in' like a parade-ground command; here 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Training is practice or physical drill, a form of exercise.

clue.text: Disconcerted indeed when not acknowledged

indicators.note: disconcerted means thrown into confusion, so the letters of indeed are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is truly put out when their efforts go unrecognised.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny something is to refuse to admit it, so denied is unacknowledged.

clue.text: Having eaten, try making an appeal

indicators.note: making means forming something new, so the letters of eaten and try are made into another word

explanation.surface: After a meal, someone has a go at pleading.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request, a plea or appeal.

clue.text: Check on the queen's canopy

parts.note: to test something is to check it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: An inspection of the monarch's state canopy.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen. A tester is the canopy over a four-poster bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester is the overhead covering on a four-poster bed or above a pulpit.

clue.text: Honours and compliments

definitions.meaning: honours as a verb means shows esteem for
compliments as in sending one's regards or polite greetings

explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to hold them in regard, and one pays one's regards as polite greetings.

clue.text: Fat Greek in need of comfort

parts.note: ease is comfort, freedom from pain or worry

explanation.surface: An overweight Greek man wants a little consolation.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is melted animal fat or oily lubricant.

clue.text: Game seaman, first-class

parts.note: fives is a British handball game played in a walled court
tar, Jack Tar, is slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor who is up for anything is top notch.
explanation.walkthrough: FIVES is a ball game hit with the hand, played at some British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-star rating is the top grade, as for luxury hotels, so excellent.

clue.text: Modish youth will accept one so decorated

parts.note: in means fashionable, modish

indicators.note: will accept means take in, so the youth word holds the one

parts.note: a lad is a youth
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A trendy young man will take on someone similarly adorned.
explanation.definitionFit: Inlaid work has pieces of another material set into its surface as ornament.

clue.text: Correct in backing in to get moving

indicators.note: the second in places the turned letters inside the moving word

parts.note: to push something is to get it moving

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word in is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a driver reversing into a space, telling them to move.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two 'in's: the first is the word that gets turned round, the second is the container signal. 'Correct' is a verb here, meaning discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct a wrongdoer in the old sense is to punish them.

clue.text: Poster ordered with all speed

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new sequence, so the letters of poster are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A placard was commissioned to be done urgently.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is a musical direction meaning very fast, and an exclamation for instant results.

clue.text: Still wanting variety

definitions.meaning: still as in nevertheless, even so

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nonetheless as a sentence adverb, and literally describes things that are identical.

clue.text: They'll support certain measures

definitions.meaning: the parts of the body that hold a person up when standing
units of length, each twelve inches

explanation.definitionFit: We stand on these body parts, and the same word names imperial units of length.

clue.text: Business is steady

definitions.meaning: a business is a company or commercial enterprise

explanation.definitionFit: A company is called a firm, and the adjective means solid and unmoving.

clue.text: Winger putting money into bag

parts.note: L stands for pound, from Latin libra, a unit of money
into shortened gives in
to bag something is to net it

explanation.surface: A footballer on the wing pockets some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer on the wing, but means a bird. L, from libra, stands for pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A linnet is a small finch, and any bird is a creature with wings.

clue.text: All object about a body of soldiers

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the object word goes round the soldiers

parts.note: an entity is a thing, an object
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of the British army

explanation.surface: Every item concerns an army regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All' is the definition as a noun, the whole of something; the Royal Engineers are a common crossword corps.
explanation.definitionFit: The entirety means the whole, everything, all of it.
